editorialMeter.label: Exploratory orientation
editorialMeter.method: 59/100 remains inherited editorial orientation, not a scientific probability. Core question reoriented to physical multiplicity of outcome histories; audit VC-006 does not find experimental branch-count discrimination in Everett/Bohm/GRW/Bell/decoherence or the separate cosmological bubble search. R006: Ten complete main-text critical source studies (read-through with assumptions and objections, not complete experimental replication) add research coverage and reproducible limited math checks, but no observation that discriminates realized Everett branch count. Audit VC-007 explicitly retains 59→59.
editorialMeter.empiricalVerdict: Unresolved: observers record one sequence, but that does not experimentally determine how many alternative quantum histories are physically real.

entries.title: Gravitational time dilation is experimentally established
entries.strength: High for time dilation, none for timeline count
entries.question: Can gravity change the passage of time?
entries.finding: Precision atomic clocks confirm relativistic time dilation. This does not demonstrate backward travel or multiple histories.
entries.source: NIST · Putting Einstein to the Test
entries.locationType: Associated institution; not a claimed experiment coordinate
entries.notes: Do not conflate established time dilation with the ability to alter the past.

entries.title: Closed timelike curves arise in some relativistic solutions
entries.question: Can general relativity admit looping worldlines?
entries.finding: Certain mathematical spacetimes contain closed timelike curves, but physical realizability and formation remain open.
entries.source: Gödel (1949) rotating cosmological solution; Hawking (1992) contrast
entries.notes: Original Gödel paper §1 p.447 and §3 p.449 constructs closed timelike paths in a specified rotating spacetime. Hawking studies constraints on forming chronology horizons from specified initial conditions, not a contradiction. Mathematical existence is not a measured machine or multiple histories. Follow-up limited independent algebra reproduced Gödel's g_phi_phi=4a²sinh²r(sinh²r−1), timelike for r>asinh(1); still only a conditional exact metric.

entries.title: Chronology protection is an unproven possibility
entries.question: Might nature prevent paradox-causing time loops?
entries.finding: Hawking argues that compactly generated Cauchy horizons from bounded local interventions encounter classical energy-condition and quantum backreaction obstacles. KRW proves Hadamard/local-field obstructions at base points; Visser argues semiclassical reliability may fail before backreaction determines the outcome. None is a universal quantum-gravity prohibition.
entries.notes: Original Hawking §§II–VI revisited, together with KRW Theorems 1/2 and Visser §§II–V; see SRC-003, SRC-055–057, NOTE-022–025 and research/field-note-003.md. Distinguish a QFT singular/undefined renormalized tensor from universal divergence of every stress component or proof of physical nonexistence.

entries.title: Quantum time-loop consistency can be modeled
entries.question: Can a quantum formalism resolve a grandfather-type contradiction?
entries.finding: Deutsch modeled quantum systems interacting with closed timelike curves under self-consistency conditions; this does not establish branch travel.
entries.source: Deutsch · Quantum mechanics near closed timelike lines (1991)
entries.notes: Deutsch 1991 Eq.15-18 p.3203 establishes a finite-dimensional fixed-point consistency condition GIVEN an assumed CTC; a maximum-entropy selection is separately proposed p.3204. Politzer 1994 and Lloyd et al. 2011 offer mathematically different conditional prescriptions (abstracts examined). No observed gravitational CTC or branch count follows. Follow-up 2x2 NOT-loop toy Phi(rho)=XrhoX has both maximally mixed and pure-state fixed points, while a deterministic Boolean NOT loop cannot; conditional algebra, not proof of CTC existence.

entries.title: Many-worlds is a viable interpretation, not a verified branch census
entries.question: Does quantum mechanics require multiple realized histories?
entries.finding: Everett, Bohmian particle configurations and objective-collapse models describe observed quantum outcomes with different physical ontologies; current reviews do not uniquely count actual branches.
entries.source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Many-Worlds Interpretation
entries.notes: See SRC-007/010/011/012/042/048/058–061; NOTE-026–030; field-note-004. The central test requires differing physical predictions, not a vote from Bell tests.

entries.title: Schrödinger's cat frames the measurement problem
entries.question: How do quantum descriptions relate to definite observations?
entries.finding: The cat thought experiment highlights the measurement problem; its alternatives are interpreted differently by competing theories.
entries.source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Quantum Mechanics
entries.notes: A thought experiment is not an observation of competing universes.

entries.title: A chronology-horizon quantum-field obstruction has narrow theorem scope
entries.direction: Neither confirms nor refutes existence of multiple physical histories
entries.strength: Rigorous conditional field-theory theorem plus model-dependent reliability analysis; no direct experiment
entries.question: Does breakdown of ordinary field-theoretic assumptions on a compactly generated chronology horizon prove physically impossible time travel?
entries.finding: KRW's linear-field results establish breakdown of F-locality and Hadamard regularity at base points, not a universal no-time-machine theorem. Visser argues that semiclassical predictions may be unreliable near this region; special modeled cases evade large mean stress before reliability fails.
entries.notes: Primary passage checks: SRC-055 (arXiv gr-qc/9603012, §§1/4/5/6), SRC-056 (arXiv gr-qc/9702041 §§II–V), SRC-057 (publisher abstract); NOTE-023–025; field-note-003. Not a proof that full quantum gravity forbids all CTCs.

entries.title: One observer record cannot establish how many physical histories are real
entries.strength: Theories can have overlapping observable predictions
entries.question: Does our physical universe contain one actual timeline or multiple physically real outcome histories?
entries.finding: One outcome stream is observed by an individual. Everettian, Bohmian and objective-collapse theories differ in ontology while sharing much empirical quantum behavior; certain collapse dynamics can be tested conditionally.
entries.source: Everett 1957, Bohm 1952, GRW 1986, Zurek 2003, loophole-free Bell 2015
entries.notes: SRC-007/010/011/012/042/048/058–061; NOTE-026–030 and field-note-004. Bell tests are not proof of branching. R006 full-source batch in research/full-study-batch-001.md, NOTE-033–042, SRC-008/012/020/044/045/047/064 and complementary SRC-002/003/062; 10 completed literature reviews, not proof of branch ontology.

entries.title: Cosmological bubble regions are not Everett quantum histories
entries.status: Specific CMB null search, no confirmed bubble
entries.question: Do other inflationary cosmological regions exist, and are they quantum branches?
entries.finding: The WMAP 7-year bubble-collision search did not warrant augmenting the reference cosmological model. Bubble regions are distinct from Everett branches; the null result does not exclude all inaccessible regions.
entries.source: Feeney et al., Physical Review Letters 2011 and Physical Review D 2015
entries.place: WMAP cosmic microwave background sky data
entries.notes: SRC-062/063, NOTE-031, field-note-004; no observed separate bubble.
